questions: Did slalom progress rise above 0.39, or did any slalom run finish?
Did slalom max_error fall below the 0.06 m floor, or is it still at about 0.0618?
Did s-bend steering_oscillation fall below 0.5 (iteration 6: 0.518) with the smaller footprint?
Did oval and s-bend finish rates hold near 0.90 and 0.65, or did the smaller footprint lose the tape at the outer sensors (line_loss_events above about 0.15 on the oval)?

intent: Keep the iteration-6 design (0.5 kg, 0.10 m track, 7 sensors at +/-0.06 m, lead 0.05 m, body 0.12 x 0.10 m) and change only the sensor footprint from 16 mm to 12 mm. The aim is to sharpen the tape-edge reading on the slalom, where max_error sits at the 0.06 m floor, and to see whether the s-bend oscillation (0.518) falls. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.39 with a first finish or more, oval finish at or above 0.90, s-bend finish at or above 0.65.
learning: Iteration 6 showed that 0.5 kg raised slalom progress (0.34 to 0.39) and oval finish (0.85 to 0.90) while the s-bend oscillation reached 0.518, close to the 0.5 threshold. The span is confirmed as adequate by the iteration-5 result, so the footprint is the last untested geometry lever. If this does not move the slalom, the remaining limit is the controller's kd or base_speed, and I will report that to the Integrator rather than change geometry further.
rationale: Iteration 6 (mass 0.5 kg, otherwise the iteration-3 geometry) is the best design so far at 586.9, up from 493.2. Its slalom progress rose from 0.34 to 0.39 with line loss 0.05 and max_error 0.0618, so the slalom is closer to finishing but still ends off track at the 0.06 m floor. The oval finish rate rose to 0.90 and s-bend finish to 0.65, and s-bend steering_oscillation is 0.518, just above the 0.5 threshold in the Integrator's rule. That rule returns to 0.6 kg only when oscillation rises above 0.5 without a slalom gain. Here the slalom did gain, so I keep 0.5 kg. Reach at +/-0.06 m is adequate (iteration 5 showed that +/-0.07 m cut progress on the slalom and s-bend), and the 0.10 m track is the best tested. The remaining untested geometry lever is the sensor footprint. I change sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m, keeping the iteration-6 span, spacing (20 mm), lead and body. A smaller footprint sharpens the tape-edge reading, which may cut the slalom max_error at the floor, and it may reduce edge-crossing jitter. The cost is a slightly smaller reach at the outer sensors, which I accept since the reach test showed the slalom is not limited by span. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.39 and some slalom finishes, with oval and s-bend finish rates holding near 0.90 and 0.65. If s-bend oscillation rises above about 0.55 or the slalom does not improve, the footprint change will be reverted to 0.016 m.
